output.methodChoice: Compared rival causes against the service and complaint records; collected X13 (service history by workshop) and X1 (Northfield job cards and stores log).
output.brief: The soft pedals are most likely caused by old, water-contaminated brake fluid put into vans at Northfield Motor Services during the bay closure, not by drivers, the Tessaro pads, or the Upper Wend hills. Eleven of the 27 complaint vans were among the Northfield vans that got fluid from an old, opened drum (boiling point about 150°C against 255°C for sealed stock). The two Northfield vans that got fresh fluid have no complaints, and Calder Road vans with the same pads have none either. Warranty checks on LK-217 and LK-224 confirmed low boiling point and a long pedal on hills. I'm fairly confident, but no one has yet tested fluid in the other eleven vans. This week: take the Northfield-serviced vans out of service, test fluid boiling point, and renew it from sealed stock before returning them. Hold off on written warnings, which would punish drivers who are reporting real faults, and on switching pad suppliers. Reply to the 25 Sep Northfield email, which recommended rechecking, is still unanswered and should be followed up.
